_what: Retrieved evidence on NR4A-family functional redundancy and on the consequences of losing NR4A3, for the paragraph the fusion-junction ASO manuscript adds to its Discussion.
_why: External review, 2026-08-15: "Nothing addresses whether wild-type NR4A3 knockdown is actually harmful — NR4A family redundancy, knockout phenotypes. The entire premise is that sparing it matters; a paragraph on how much would strengthen the framing either way." Correct, and the whole modality is justified by the premise that sparing wild-type NR4A3 is worth the specificity cost, which the paper had never examined.
_what_this_is_not: Not a fetch performed from recollection. Every field and every quote is copied from a Europe PMC core record retrieved by fetch-literature.yml and committed on the literature-cache branch at the revision named in `source`; each quote is asserted to appear verbatim in that record's abstract before this file is written, and the build FAILS if one does not.
Not a statement about EMC. Every record here is haematopoietic or vascular. Whether NR4A3 loss is tolerated in the tissue an EMC arises in is not addressed by any of them, and the manuscript says so.
Not a safety assessment. Nothing here is a study of an oligonucleotide, a knockdown, or a dose.
Not exhaustive. These are the records this repository already held that bear on the question; a broader NR4A loss-of-function sweep was dispatched alongside and is a separate corpus.
_cost: $0 — one CI dispatch on a free runner for author metadata, over records already committed here.

29343483.title: NR4A1 and NR4A3 restrict HSC proliferation via reciprocal regulation of C/EBPα and inflammatory signaling.
quotes_verbatim_from_the_retrieved_abstr: We previously identified NR4A1 and NR4A3 (NR4A1/3) as functionally redundant suppressors of acute myeloid leukemia (AML) development.

Using a conditional Nr4a1/Nr4a3 knockout mouse (CDKO), we show that codepletion of NR4A1/3 promotes acute changes in HSC homeostasis including loss of HSC quiescence, accumulation of oxidative stress, and DNA damage while maintaining stem cell regenerative and differentiation capacity.

21205929.title: Reduced NR4A gene dosage leads to mixed myelodysplastic/myeloproliferative neoplasms in mice.
21205929.authorString: Ramirez-Herrick AM, Mullican SE, Sheehan AM, Conneely OM.
quotes_verbatim_from_the_retrieved_abstr: We previously discovered that 2 of these receptors, NR4A1 and NR4A3, are potent tumor suppressors of acute myeloid leukemia (AML); they are silenced in human AML, and abrogation of both genes in mice leads to rapid postnatal development of AML.

Here we show that reduced gene dosage of NR4A1 and NR4A3 in hypoallelic (NR4A1(+/-)NR4A3(-/-) or NR4A1(-/-)NR4A3(+/-)) mice below a critical threshold leads to a chronic myeloid malignancy that closely recapitulates the pathologic features of mixed myelodysplastic/myeloproliferative neoplasms (MDS/MPNs)

Additionally, NR4A1 and NR4A3 (Nor-1) are described as tumor suppressors in leukemia.
